page: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v7 is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine configured with a reduced memory-to-vCPU footprint and high-speed local temporary storage. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance runs on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked up to 4.2 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 dedicated virtual CPUs spanning 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, accompanied by 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a lean 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware vector capabilities include AVX, AVX-512, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

Local ephemeral storage is provided via a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD, avoiding network-attached storage latency for scratch datasets, while no discrete GPU acceleration is included. Benchmark measurements show solid single-threaded computational efficiency, highlighted by top-tier single-threaded compression performance with gzip reaching 36.23 GB/sec and bzip3 reaching 14.92 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput on stress-ng and bzip3 falls into the lower quartile, reflecting the physical two-core constraint under saturated multi-threaded parallel workloads.

Memory throughput registers moderately under uncached read sweeps at 43.66 GB/sec, while write operations and cached block transfers exhibit lower relative bandwidth. Database operations such as Redis SET achieve typical throughput of 8.31 million operations per second, and static web serving achieves 8.67 GB/sec. Larger memory-resident operations such as 7B model LLM inference yield minimal throughput due to the restricted 8.0 GB capacity and core count.

From an infrastructure perspective, the D4lds_v7 provides resource efficiency for organizations requiring local fast NVMe disk and high single-core CPU frequency without paying for surplus RAM. The instance fits lightweight web servers, intermediate CI/CD build agents, batch processing pipelines with low memory footprints, and stateless container hosts using fast local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v7 is a compute-focused general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 8.0 GB of memory. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features a low 2.0 GB per vCPU memory allocation paired with a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD for fast local ephemeral storage. Hardware vector capabilities include AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong single-threaded throughput, reaching 36.23 GB/sec in gzip compression, while multi-core workloads and memory write operations show moderate to weak relative scalability. The VM lacks dedicated GPU acceleration and complimentary public IPv4 networking. The D4lds_v7 is well structured for lightweight web serving, caching proxies, stateless batch tasks, and CI/CD compile stages requiring high-speed local disk IOPS without large memory overhead.
